question: Describe your enterprise security, privacy, accessibility, and AI-governance organization, including executive accountability.
Provide your NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5 control crosswalk and identify implemented, partial, planned, and independently assessed controls.
Describe your risk-assessment process for new integrations, new AI models, source expansion, and official-write workflows.
Provide your security, privacy, data-retention, incident-response, business-continuity, accessibility, secure-development, and vendor-risk policies.
Identify all subprocessors, including cloud hosting, analytics, support, AI/model vendors, integrations, and communications vendors.
Describe subprocessor approval, review, contractual controls, customer notice, and removal processes.
Describe your software release/change-control process for integrations, models, prompts, policies, and agents.
Identify all certifications, independent assessments, penetration tests, and accessibility assessments currently available.
Which identity standards are supported: SAML 2.0, OpenID Connect, OAuth 2.0, SCIM 2.0, MFA, passkeys, and delegated administration?
Describe provisioning, role changes, suspension, transfer, deprovisioning, and account- recovery flows.
Describe RBAC and ABAC enforcement across institution, campus, college, program, course, term, workflow, data class, purpose, and consent scope.
Explain how least privilege applies to users, staff, support personnel, services, API credentials, AI agents, and tool calls.
Describe administrative MFA, break-glass access, privileged-session logging, and periodic access review.
Explain tenant isolation for relational data, files, caches, semantic/vector indexes, logs, analytics, backups, and model context.
Describe support-staff access controls, customer approval requirements, session recording/logging, and emergency access procedures.
Identify the exact 1EdTech standards and versions supported: LTI 1.3, LTI Advantage, NRPS, AGS, Deep Linking, OneRoster, Edu-API, CASE, QTI, Caliper, Common Cartridge, Open Badges.
Provide a feature-by-feature conformance matrix, limitations, and test/conformance evidence for each claimed standard.
Describe LTI 1.3 OIDC login and launch validation: issuer, audience, deployment ID, nonce, state, JWT signature, JWKS rotation, redirect URI, and time-window validation.
Describe LTI registration storage, tenant separation, platform key management, secret rotation, and revocation.
Describe how LTI roster/membership data from NRPS is scoped, minimized, cached, refreshed, expired, and deleted.
Describe AGS grade passback safeguards: institutional enablement, course/faculty approval, user role enforcement, preview, confirmation, idempotency, reconciliation, rollback, and audit.
Describe Deep Linking authorization, content/source versioning, instructor controls, and change history.
Describe OneRoster support, including version, CSV/REST options, supported objects, sync handling, field-level minimization, and error recovery.
Describe Edu-API entity support, canonical model mapping, transformation versioning, source ownership, validation, and vendor-adapter architecture.
Identify all integration methods—API, events, webhook, SFTP, CSV, direct database, manual import—and state whether direct production database access is ever required.
Describe integration service-account scopes, OAuth controls, secrets storage, key rotation, rate limits, input validation, retries, queues, dead-letter handling, and reconciliation.
Describe behavior during LMS/SIS outages, including stale-data labels, safe mode, write prevention, user notices, and recovery.
Provide a complete data-processing inventory by data class, integration, source, purpose, recipient, region, retention, access role, model/AI eligibility, and deletion method.
Describe how authority to process PII and PII processing purpose are recorded and technically enforced for every workflow and agent.
Describe how the platform distinguishes institution-required processing from optional student consent.
Describe consent collection, granular scopes, accessibility, language clarity, expiration, revocation, policy versioning, audit history, and downstream enforcement.
Can students view data used in recommendations, decision workspaces, tutoring, advisor packets, and AI answers? Provide product evidence.
Describe student controls for access, export, correction requests, deletion of eligible personal content, sharing, recipient-specific access, expiration, and revocation.
Identify data categories excluded from routine AI retrieval by default.
Describe protections for grades, transcript, enrollment status, degree-audit data, instructor feedback, academic standing, and private advising notes.
Describe protections for financial-aid, payment, accommodation, health/counseling, conduct, immigration, identity-document, emergency-contact, and disciplinary information.

Confirm whether student notes, tutor sessions, course activity, attendance, search history, or workspace content are used for grading, discipline, admissions, financial aid, employment, marketing, behavioral profiling, or model training.
Describe retention and deletion controls for customer records, files, prompts, outputs, vector indexes, integration caches, operational logs, backups, and legal holds.
Describe data residency, cross-border processing, location selection, and subprocessor region controls.
Describe privacy incident intake, investigation, notification, remediation, and redress processes.
List every model/provider used, deployment location, API/service type, retention/data-use terms, training policy, and subprocessor relationship.
State whether student/institution data, prompts, attachments, tool outputs, or generated outputs may train shared or proprietary models.
Describe the AI Gateway, including source authorization, data classification, purpose checks, consent enforcement, model routing, logging, and human escalation.
Describe agent boundaries for Executive Assistant, Executive Advisor, Tutor, Course Guide, and any workflow agents.
Describe safeguards against prompt injection, indirect prompt injection from sources/files, data exfiltration, cross-user context leakage, tool abuse, source poisoning, and autonomous writes.
Describe source grounding, citation/provenance, source freshness, uncertainty handling, missing-source handling, and source-owner correction workflows.
Describe course- and activity-level academic-integrity enforcement, including restricted assessments, AI policy configuration, student notices, and faculty controls.

Describe prohibited AI uses, including automated high-impact decisions, student surveillance, hidden risk scoring, discipline, eligibility decisions, and unapproved grade and academic integrity inference.
Describe human oversight, student confirmation, staff approval, two-person approvals, action limits, kill switches, and rollback for official workflows.

Provide evidence from AI evaluation, red-team, or adversarial testing for privacy, prompt injection, policy compliance, hallucination, academic integrity, accessibility, bias, security, and harmful advice.
Describe AI trace logging: prompt/input categories, sources retrieved, policy decision, model/version, tools used, output, confirmation, approval, and retention/access safeguards.
Describe encryption in transit and at rest, key hierarchy, KMS/HSM use, key rotation, backup encryption, and customer-managed-key options.
Describe secure SDLC controls: threat modeling, design review, code review, SAST, DAST, dependency and secret scanning, SBOM, pen testing, and remediation timelines.
Describe vulnerability management, disclosure process, severity definitions, patch SLA, exception process, and customer notification.
Describe event logging for authentication, access decisions, sensitive reads, exports, consent changes, policy edits, configuration changes, integration activity, AI/tool calls, and official writes.
Describe SIEM export, log API, retention, immutability, tamper detection, clock synchronization, and correlation identifiers.
Describe security/privacy/AI incident-response plan, severity tiers, notification timelines, forensic support, lessons learned, and tabletop testing.
Provide tested RTO/RPO, backup frequency, restore-test cadence, regional-failure strategy, capacity planning, and peak registration/exam resilience.
Describe integration reliability controls: idempotency, dead-letter queues, message replay, reconciliation, circuit breakers, rate limiting, and duplicate-write protection.
Describe customer exit: data export formats, migration assistance, source mapping, retention after termination, secure deletion, and certificate-of-deletion.
Provide a current VPAT/Accessibility Conformance Report, standards used, assessment date, known gaps, and remediation timeline.
Describe how accessibility is tested for mobile, keyboard-only workflows, screen readers, low vision, color contrast, captions, documents, generated content, tables, charts, and math.
Describe implementation phases, institutional governance setup, integration onboarding, source validation, data-mapping review, training, and support model.
Describe the controls and institutional approvals required before enabling “Operate” mode or any official-record write.
Identify known limitations against this RFP’s security, privacy, accessibility, interoperability, retention, residency, or procurement requirements.
